neighbours.label: verb or participle right after a plural noun subject that links it to its cause, outcome or form ('injuries caused by', 'infections result in', 'words ending in', 'cases originate in'); the same nouns with an ordinary predicate stay low
fire: Doctors say that most burns caused by hot water happen in the kitchen.
In this lesson, verbs ending in -ing are treated as gerunds.
Fortunately, only a few bee stings result in a severe allergic reaction.
Experts believe many house fires originate in faulty wiring.
The report notes that crashes caused by fatigue are rising on highways.
Teachers explain that adjectives ending in -ous often come from Latin.
In the trial, few vaccine doses resulted in any side effects.
Engineers found that most leaks originate in the older pipes.
quiet: Doctors say that most burns heal well if they are kept clean.
In this lesson, verbs are printed in bold for the students.
Fortunately, only a few bee stings were reported at the picnic.
Experts believe many house fires are reported late at night.
The report notes that crashes on highways are listed by month.
Teachers explain that adjectives are useful for describing people.
In the trial, few vaccine doses were stored in the warm room.
Engineers found that most pipes were painted blue years ago.
